speed.definition: per video: sum of the wall-clock of each stage run on that video; ratio = that sum / video duration (src_frames / 30). All videos in the denominator, failures included. Summed stage time, not one measured file-to-output interval; download excluded.

metrics.bootstrap_scope: Sequence-level bootstrap: resamples the scored sequences with replacement, conditional on this fitted pipeline and these realized predictions. It does not cover the development choices (prompts, thresholds, cascade rules selected on labeled dev videos), provider sampling noise (one execution), other laboratories, setups, or species. It treats sequences as independent units, which is not verified (consecutive test sequences may share animals or sessions).

targets_check.rule: Higher-is-better: MET if the point estimate is >= the threshold; MET ROBUSTLY if the 95% sequence-bootstrap CI lower bound is also >= it. Lower-is-better: MET if the point is <= the threshold; MET ROBUSTLY if the CI upper bound is also <= it. A metric without a CI can be MET, never MET ROBUSTLY. Anything else is NOT MET. No rounding: compared at full precision.
targets_check.level_rule: An accuracy level (minimum_credible or good) is reached only if macro F1 AND each of the three per-behavior F1 thresholds are MET (robustly only if all four are MET ROBUSTLY). Every other target (tier-1 lift, speed, cost, identity, coverage) is a separate verdict; there is no single overall 'success'. 'Minimum credible' is an engineering milestone, not a scientific validation threshold.

minimum_credible.note: no CI for speed: MET ROBUSTLY is not applicable

good.note: no CI for speed: MET ROBUSTLY is not applicable
